header.title: PGM VIII: Binding love spell of Astrampsychus and a request for a dream oracle of Besas: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Papyri Graecae Magicae
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:dclp:59324:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.3.89: ‘(the usual)’ renders κοι(νόν), the handbook’s instruction to add the usual formula. In 3.99 the scribe also wrote, and deleted, a misspelt ‘rise up’.
notes.1.26: ‘(the usual)’ renders κοιν(όν), the handbook’s instruction to add the usual formula.
notes.2.46: ‘May you turn the scale [for me]’ renders the uncertain συνρέποις. ‘Now, now, quickly, quickly’ renders ‘now 2, quickly 2’.
notes.1.1: The papyrus spells the name Astrapsoukos (the title’s Astrampsychus); the first word is partly uncertain.

nodes.text: Binding love spell of Astrapsoukos. (Formula):
Come to me, lord Hermes, as babies [come] into the wombs of women.
Come to me, lord Hermes, who gather the sustenance of (gods)
cosmos, the living creatures; so I too, (NN), call on you. Therefore give
me favour, form, beauty; hear me, Hermes,
benefactor, ⟨inventor⟩ of drugs, be gracious in speech and hear [me],
just as you did everything for your Ethiopian dog-headed baboon,
the lord of those beneath the earth. Calm everyone and give me
strength, form (the usual), and let them give me gold and silver
and all food without fail. Keep me safe
always, forever, from drugs and treacheries
and every evil eye and wicked tongues, from
every constraint, from all hatred of gods and men.
Let them give me favour and victory and success and plenty. For you
are I and I am you; your (name) is mine and mine is yours; for I am the
days of the rising of the (moon); and the second (name) has
the number 7, [that] of the rulers of the world,
with the numerical value 365, corresponding to the days of the
year. Truly: Abrasax. I know you, Hermes, and you [know] me.
I am you and you are I. So do everything for me, and
may you turn the scale [for me] with Good Fortune and the Good Daimon,
now, now, quickly, quickly.
Taking olive wood, make a small baboon, seated,
burn frankincense on it, and set it wherever you wish in the workshop,
in the middle. The (name) to be written is: phthoron phthionē Thōuth;
write besides these great (names) too: Iaō Sabaōth
Adōnaie ablanath(analba) akrammach(amarei), 365, give to the workshop
business, favour, prosperity, charm,
to NN himself and to the workshop, now, now, quickly, quickly.
you, saying the (formula), and he will come to you. Keep very near you
a tablet, so that you may write down whatever he says, so that you do not, falling asleep,
forget. I call on you, the headless (god), who at your
feet have your sight, who flash lightning
and thunder. You are the one whose mouth is continually full of fire,
the one set over Necessity. I call
on you, the (god) set over Necessity,
Iaeō Sabaōth Adōnai Zabarbathiaō; you are the one who
lies on the coffin of myrrh, having under your
elbow resin and asphalt, whom they call: Anouth
Anouth, rise up, *daimōn* [spirit]; you are not a *daimōn*, but the blood
of the two hawks that at the head of Osiris
chatter and keep watch. You are the oracle-giving
(god) Salbanachambrē Anouth Anouth Sabaōth Adōnai
iē ie iē ie (the usual). And sleep on a rush mat, with
an unbaked brick at your head. And what
you draw is this: a naked man, standing, with a royal
crown on his head, and in his right hand
a sword lying curved against his neck, and in
his left a staff. If he gives you an oracle, with rose
perfume wipe off your hand. And this is the figure
of the rite:
